Subject: Notice: Elevated 5xx/timeouts for model-rw-lg-1 — incident being investigated

Hi Susan and Acme ops team,

Heads up — starting ~08:05 PT we're seeing an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout errors for requests routed to model-rw-lg-1 for customers pinned to that runtime. Our monitoring shows around a 12% error rate for that model over the past 10 minutes (affecting both synchronous generation and streaming). Impact appears limited to customer requests routed to that exact model+runtime combination; other model families are unaffected.

What we're doing now:
- Engineering is actively investigating root cause (eng team paged).
- Traffic is being routed away from the affected runtime to compatible fallback variants where possible.
- We're applying conservative rate-limits for large-batch requests to reduce error amplification.

Immediate customer impact: transient 5xx/timeouts for some requests to rw-lg-1. No evidence of data leakage.

We'll follow up with more detail within the hour and share a ticket link and timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your production flows.

Subject: RE: Notice: Elevated 5xx/timeouts for model-rw-lg-1 — initial findings and mitigation

Hi all — quick technical update from the engineering side.

Summary of root cause (interim):
- Around 08:00 PT we rolled a runtime kernel selection tweak to improve throughput for rw-lg-1 on certain GPU types. The change inadvertently selected a non-ideal attention kernel path for a subset of sequence lengths, which caused increased memory spikes and GC-like stalls in our runtime for some requests.
- The stalls manifested as timeouts at the HTTP layer and returned 5xx to clients. The behavior was concentrated on the runtime variant serving rw-lg-1 on G4x hosts (shard pool 7).

Mitigations applied (08:25–08:40 PT):
- Immediate rollback of the kernel selection tweak for the affected pool (traffic returned to the previous kernel path).
- Proactive routing handshake: requests pinned to rw-lg-1 were routed to compatible fallback variants where possible; failing requests now receive a clear 429/503 guidance rather than ambiguous timeouts while we normalize.
- Autoscaler thresholds adjusted to add headroom to the impacted pool to reduce queuing.

Current status: error rate has dropped from ~12% to ~1.4% in the last 10 minutes; tail latency improving. We're keeping an elevated watch with 1-minute metrics and increased logging for the affected pool.

Next steps:
- Full log collection and correlation (ongoing).
- Postmortem with timeline and root-cause analysis to be shared within 48 hours.
- We'll propose long-term mitigations (improved kernel selection tests, canary gating).

If Acme wants us to roll back all pinned customers off rw-lg-1 temporarily or to open a dedicated technical call, happy to schedule.

- Sean
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Postmortem and next steps for rw-lg-1 incident (INC-20260210-rw-lg1)

Hi Susan — thank you again for the patience. We've attached the postmortem and the runtime rollout log. The postmortem includes a minute-by-minute timeline, root cause analysis, and recommended actions. Highlights:

- Root cause: an overly permissive kernel-selection gate allowed a new attention kernel to be used for certain sequence-length distributions; under real traffic patterns this kernel caused memory allocation spikes and rare stalls, which surfaced as timeouts (5xx) at the HTTP layer.
- Scope: customers pinned to model-rw-lg-1 on the affected runtime pool (G4x, shard pool 7). We estimate ~4% of production requests across affected tenants saw transient errors between 08:05–08:40 PT.
- Mitigation completed: rollback at 08:25 PT; routing and autoscaler headroom applied; monitoring confirmed stabilization by 09:05 PT.
- Customer-facing recommendations: we recommend customers avoid pinning to a single runtime variant when consistent low-tail latency is required; instead configure fallback variants in routing policies. For Acme specifically, we propose a short window to move pinned traffic to rw-lg-1-compat (a validated fallback) — we can do this on your behalf.

Attachments:
- redwood_model_incident_postmortem_20260210.pdf (postmortem, timeline, remediation plan)
- rw-lg1-runtime-rollout-log-20260210.log (rollout logs & kernel selection traces)

Links:
- Incident status: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-20260210-rw-lg1
- Shared postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/postmortems/rw-lg1-20260210
- Support ticket: https://acmeai.zendesk.com/tickets/78921

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute technical review with the runtime team to walk through the postmortem and recommendations? If yes, please suggest times and we'll coordinate.

Thanks — we own the follow-through here and will implement the deferred mitigations from the remediation plan.

Best,
